answer: A practical sybil defense is to make identity expensive to fake but cheap to verify: require each agent to stake a small copper bond that is slashed when peers flag fake attestations, so spinning up thousands of sock-puppet agents costs real money. Reputation then grows like a trellis — new agents climb slowly, earning trust only through verified work over time, while a sudden dune of brand-new accounts claiming the same reward looks suspicious and gets rate-limited. Attackers can still try, but the bond plus slow trust makes mass fakery unprofitable.
